 Bangladesh Records 427 Deaths from Dengue Fever and More Than 6,000 Injuries
 Monday 02 November 2026 - Time: 09:46 
 SadaNews - The health authorities in Bangladesh announced that the death toll from dengue fever has risen to 427 since the beginning of 2026, following the registration of 8 new deaths and 1,929 hospital admissions in the last 24 hours. The country continues to face the spread of the disease after recording the highest monthly death toll in October. 
 According to data from the "Directorate General of Health Services" reported by "BD News 24" on Sunday, the total number of hospital admissions due to the disease reached 136,929 cases since the beginning of the year, with 130,388 patients discharged after receiving treatment.
 The data indicated that October recorded 174 deaths from dengue fever, making it the month with the highest deaths since the beginning of the year, compared to 148 deaths in September.
 The "Daily Star" reported, based on official health data, that 6,114 patients are still receiving treatment in hospitals across the country.
 Dhaka Division recorded the highest number of new hospital admissions, with 831 cases from Saturday morning to Sunday morning, followed by Khulna Division with 259 cases, and Chittagong with 257 cases.
 Other cases were distributed across Barisal Division with 213 cases, Rajshahi with 185 cases, Mymensingh with 92 cases, Rangpur with 73 cases, and Sylhet with 19 cases, reflecting the spread of the disease in various regions of the country.
 The official figures refer to hospital admissions and do not necessarily include all dengue fever cases, as some infections may go unnoticed or present mild symptoms not requiring hospitalization.
 Bangladesh's health authorities have been maintaining records of admissions and deaths related to dengue fever since 2000.
 The country experienced its worst recorded outbreak of the disease in 2023, when the number of hospital admissions reached 321,179, with 1,705 deaths, according to data from "BD News 24".
 Despite the rise in deaths last October, the recorded toll since the beginning of 2026 remains lower than the figures during the outbreak in 2023.
 Dengue fever is a viral disease primarily transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes, and it particularly spreads in tropical and subtropical regions.
 The "World Health Organization" estimates that about half of the world's population is at risk of contracting the disease, with an estimated 100 million to 400 million infections occurring annually worldwide.
 The organization clarifies that most infections do not cause symptoms or result in mild symptoms, although some cases may develop into severe disease that poses life-threatening risks.
 Common symptoms include fever, headache, body aches, nausea, and rash, while signs of severe infection may appear after fever subsides.
 Key danger signs include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, rapid breathing, and bleeding, which are symptoms requiring urgent medical care.
 The "World Health Organization" emphasizes that early diagnosis and provision of proper medical care contribute to reducing deaths due to severe cases, even though there is no specific treatment that eliminates the virus itself.
 According to the "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention", four closely related viral serotypes can cause dengue fever, meaning that recovery from a previous infection does not provide complete protection against subsequent infections.
